ergo quo tempore Tatari Moguli
Mesopotamiam & Syriam pervaserunt, quorum res ges-
tas tradit à Ingiscban ( qui occiso Vng-Chan,
eo qui ﻭﺣﻧﺎ ﻣﻠﻚ Rex Iuhanna, seu Iohannes,
dictus est, è tribu ﻛﺮﻳﺖ Carrit, quae Chri-
stianam professa est religionem, ad imperi-
um evectus est circa annum Alex. 1514.
Hejrae 599.) usque ad Abaga Il-Chan, anno
Hejrae 675. ( quo tempore obiit Nasiroddi-
nus Tusiensis, Philosophus & Mathematicus
insignis,) vel, ut in altero exemplari, usque ad
Argun Il-Chan; anno Hejrae 683, Alex. 1596.
Historiam autem suam, quam in decem {*} Dy-
nastias divisit, contexuisse se scribit ex eo-
rum qui hoc in genere diversis linguis, Sy-
riacâ scil. Arabica, aliisque scripserunt, monu-
mentis. In priore ejus parte, secutum se ait,
Eusebium,& Andronicum Chronologos, quòd
cum iis convenisse videret, eruditissimo Viro
Iacobo Robawien.si, trium linguarum Hebrai-
cae scil. Graecae & Syriacae peritiâ insigni. In eâ
quae Arabes & Mohammedanos spectat, secu-
tus praecipuè videtur Saedum quendam, Ebn
Ahmed

page.notes: Arabic and Greek text in the margins and in the body is transcribed as far as legible; the Arabic in the top-left margin and the Arabic words in the body (ﻟﻲ ﺯﻣﺎﺩ, ﻭﺣﻧﺎ ﻣﻠﻚ, ﻛﺮﻳﺖ) and the Arabic heading of the third note are uncertain and should be checked against the scan. The Arabic note beside "unde nomine" reads مختصر الدول, transcribed here only as a reference. The first "*" is a reference mark that may belong to a note in the margin. Doubtful readings: "eruditissimo" (possibly printed with long s and a damaged letter), "Vng-Chan", "Rex Iuhanna". The note "i. e. Compendium Dynastiarum, nota est." is printed in the left margin under the Arabic note and belongs to the same mark.
